basic_information.name: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
basic_information.creator: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
basic_information.description: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is a fully managed RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) service on AWS that automates the entire RAG workflow — from document ingestion and chunking to embedding, vector storage, retrieval, and LLM-augmented response generation. It connects to enterprise data sources (S3, Confluence, Salesforce, SharePoint, web crawlers), supports multiple vector store backends (OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora PostgreSQL, Pinecone, MongoDB Atlas, Redis, Neptune Analytics, S3 Vectors), and provides built-in citation/source attribution, reranking, GraphRAG, multimodal retrieval, and structured data querying. As part of the broader Amazon Bedrock platform, it integrates natively with AWS services and supports multiple foundation models for embedding and generation, making it a turnkey solution for enterprises already invested in the AWS ecosystem.
basic_information.release_date: November 28, 2023 (GA at AWS re:Invent 2023; preview since September 2023)
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary managed service. AWS provides open-source samples at github.com/aws-samples/amazon-bedrock-rag and github.com/aws-samples/amazon-bedrock-samples

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Serverless, fully managed cloud service. Bedrock Knowledge Bases orchestrates ingestion (parsing, chunking, embedding) and retrieval (vector search, reranking, LLM generation) as a serverless pipeline. Users choose a vector store backend (serverless or provisioned) and the service manages the data flow between components. Supports both synchronous Retrieve/RetrieveAndGenerate APIs and integration with Bedrock Agents for agentic workflows.
technical_architecture.language: Service is cloud-managed (internal implementation not disclosed). SDKs available in Python (boto3), JavaScript, Java, .NET, Go, and other AWS SDK languages. Infrastructure-as-code via CloudFormation and Terraform.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Depends on chosen embedding model: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 supports 256, 384, and 1024 dimensions; Cohere Embed English/Multilingual v3 supports 1024 dimensions; Cohere Embed v4 supports 256-1536 dimensions (configurable). Binary vector support available with OpenSearch Serverless and OpenSearch Managed Cluster backends.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Depends on the chosen vector store backend: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless uses HNSW (nmslib/Faiss); Aurora PostgreSQL uses pgvector (IVFFlat/HNSW); Pinecone uses proprietary indexing; MongoDB Atlas uses HNSW; Redis uses HNSW; Amazon Neptune Analytics uses graph-native indexing for GraphRAG; Amazon S3 Vectors uses an optimized storage-first vector index designed for infrequent query workloads.
technical_architecture.scalability: Highly scalable through AWS infrastructure. S3 Vectors supports trillions of vectors at sub-second latency. OpenSearch Serverless auto-scales compute. Neptune Analytics handles billions of graph edges. Multi-tenancy supported through AWS IAM, resource policies, and separate knowledge base instances. No hard-coded vector count limits for the service itself — constrained by the chosen vector store backend.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cloud-managed only (AWS). Available in most AWS commercial regions. FedRAMP High authorized in AWS GovCloud (US-West). No self-hosted option. Accessible via AWS Console, AWS CLI, SDKs, and APIs. Infrastructure-as-code deployment via CloudFormation and Terraform.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector search (default), hybrid search (dense + BM25/sparse) supported with OpenSearch Serverless, OpenSearch Managed Cluster, Aurora PostgreSQL, and MongoDB Atlas. GraphRAG with Neptune Analytics for entity-relationship-enhanced retrieval. Structured data retrieval via natural language to SQL translation for querying relational databases. Multimodal retrieval across text, images, audio, and video.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Fixed-size chunking, semantic chunking, hierarchical chunking, and no chunking (use documents as-is). Custom chunking via AWS Lambda functions for full control. Integration with LangChain and LlamaIndex chunking components for off-the-shelf strategies. Advanced parsing with Foundation Model-based document parsing for complex layouts, tables, and images.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranking with Amazon Rerank v1.0 model. Reranker calculates relevance scores for each retrieved chunk relative to the query. Supports reranking across text, visual, and multimedia content. Pricing: $1.00 per 1,000 queries (each query supports up to 100 document chunks; exceeding 100 chunks counts as additional queries).
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: GA since November 2025. Supports retrieval across text, images, audio, and video files. Enables building search and Q&A applications that retrieve information from multiple modalities. Uses multimodal embedding models to index and retrieve non-text content. Example: querying 'show me Q1 projections' can retrieve relevant text, charts, video snippets, and audio segments.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Built-in GraphRAG via Amazon Neptune Analytics integration. After initial vector retrieval, the system identifies and retrieves related graph nodes linked to initially retrieved document chunks, then traverses the graph structure to gather additional context about entities and their relationships. BMW Group is a notable user of GraphRAG for their internal AI assistant (MAIA). Automated graph modeling from documents.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in source attribution and citation generation. All responses from RetrieveAndGenerate API include citations linking each claim back to the original source document and specific passage. Citations include document URI, content excerpt, and relevance metadata. Creates an audit trail for verifying every piece of information. Only cites sources relevant to the query. Visual citations also supported for multimodal content.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Custom prompt templates for RetrieveAndGenerate API to control how retrieved context is assembled. Configurable maximum number of retrieved results per query. Metadata filtering to narrow retrieval scope. Query reformulation for improved retrieval relevance. Latency-optimized model inference available for Claude 3.5 Haiku, Llama 3.1 405B/70B. Session context management for multi-turn conversations.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Varies by vector store backend and configuration. S3 Vectors delivers sub-second query latency for most datasets. OpenSearch Serverless typically provides single-digit millisecond vector search latency. End-to-end RetrieveAndGenerate latency depends heavily on the chosen LLM (generation is the bottleneck). AWS recommends monitoring p50, p95, p99, p999 latency distributions via CloudWatch. Latency-optimized inference available for select models. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Not publicly benchmarked as a single metric. Throughput depends on vector store choice: OpenSearch Serverless auto-scales for high-throughput workloads; S3 Vectors is optimized for infrequent query workloads rather than high QPS; Aurora PostgreSQL and Pinecone offer their own throughput characteristics. AWS recommends load testing with peak query simulations. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: S3 Vectors achieves 90%+ average recall. Built-in RAG evaluation capability with 13 quality evaluators (via AgentCore Evaluations) measuring retrieval relevance, faithfulness, answer correctness, and other dimensions. AWS recommends evaluating with RAGAS framework (faithfulness, context relevance, answer relevance) via integration with LlamaIndex. No single published MTEB or BEIR score since the system is a pipeline, not a single model.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: No standardized public benchmark (e.g., ANN-Benchmarks) for the full managed service. Performance depends on embedding model choice (Titan v2, Cohere Embed v4 have their own MTEB rankings) and vector store backend. AWS publishes evaluation guides recommending custom benchmarking with organization-specific data and queries. S3 Vectors GA announcement (Dec 2025) cited 40x scale improvement over preview, with sub-second latency and 90%+ recall. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Native integrations with LangChain (Python and JS), LlamaIndex (AmazonKnowledgeBasesRetriever), and RAGAS for evaluation. AWS Strands Agents framework support. Compatible with CrewAI, LangGraph, Google ADK, and OpenAI Agents SDK via Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. Terraform and CloudFormation for infrastructure-as-code. AWS CDK support.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Multi-provider model access through Amazon Bedrock: Anthropic Claude (3.5 Sonnet, 3.5 Haiku, Opus), Meta Llama (3.1, 3.2, 3.3), Amazon Titan, Mistral AI, Cohere Command R/R+, AI21 Jamba, Stability AI. Embedding models: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, Cohere Embed v3/v4. Over 100 foundation models available on the Bedrock platform. Latency-optimized inference for select models.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support available through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. AgentCore provides a serverless runtime for deploying agents using any open-source framework and any protocol including MCP.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Amazon S3 (primary), Confluence (basic and OAuth 2.0 auth), Salesforce, Microsoft SharePoint, Web Crawler (custom URL crawling with inclusion/exclusion filters). Amazon Kendra GenAI Index for enterprise search integration. Structured data sources via natural language to SQL. All connectors support granular inclusion/exclusion filters. Note: Confluence, SharePoint, and Salesforce connectors currently only support OpenSearch Serverless as the vector store.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Amazon CloudWatch for runtime metrics (InvocationLatency, token counts). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability for tracing, debugging, and monitoring agent workflows with unified operational dashboards. OpenTelemetry compatible telemetry. Integration with Arize Phoenix, Weights & Biases Weave, Langfuse. Model invocation logging to S3 queryable via Amazon Athena.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: No charge for the Knowledge Bases feature itself. Pay-as-you-go for underlying components: (1) Embedding model inference (per input token), (2) Vector store costs (varies by backend), (3) LLM generation costs (per input/output token), (4) Optional reranking ($1.00 per 1,000 queries). S3 Vectors offers storage-based pricing with no idle compute. Data ingestion and synchronization costs depend on document volume and parsing complexity.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Amazon Bedrock offers limited free tier for some models (varies by model provider). S3 Vectors has S3 standard pricing tiers. OpenSearch Serverless has no meaningful free tier (minimum ~$350/month for small workloads). New AWS accounts may qualify for Bedrock free trial credits. No dedicated free tier specifically for Knowledge Bases.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Key cost drivers at scale: (1) OpenSearch Serverless minimum footprint ~$350/month even for small workloads; (2) S3 Vectors offers up to 90% cost savings vs traditional vector databases for large datasets; (3) Reranking at $1.00/1,000 queries (each query up to 100 chunks); (4) Embedding costs: Titan V2 at ~$0.00002/1K tokens, Cohere Embed at ~$0.0001/1K tokens; (5) LLM generation: varies widely (Claude 3.5 Sonnet ~$3/$15 per 1M input/output tokens). For 1M documents: expect $500-2,000+/month depending on query volume and model choices. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Full TCO includes: vector store infrastructure (OpenSearch Serverless ~$350+/month minimum, or S3 Vectors for cost optimization), embedding model inference for ingestion and queries, LLM inference for generation, optional reranking fees, S3 storage for source documents, data transfer costs, CloudWatch monitoring, and optional Kendra GenAI Index ($0.65-1.40 per document/month). Hidden costs: OpenSearch Serverless idle compute, re-ingestion on schema changes, and reranking query multiplication for large chunk sets. S3 Vectors dramatically reduces vector store TCO for infrequent-query workloads.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the managed RAG service category within the AWS ecosystem. Part of the broader Amazon Bedrock platform which powers generative AI for 100,000+ organizations worldwide, with 4.7x customer base growth in one year. Dominant position among AWS-native organizations. Competes as one of the 'big three' cloud RAG services alongside Azure AI Search/Azure OpenAI and Google Vertex AI Search.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: BMW Group (GraphRAG for MAIA internal AI assistant), Robinhood (AI-first financial services, 5 billion tokens/day), Octus (credit intelligence, structured data retrieval), Applaud (HR platform with Claude-powered RAG), Verizon (enterprise connectivity and GenAI), Teradata (rapid-start GenAI use cases), Zendesk, Adobe, Symbeo, Tenovos, Argo Labs. Tens of thousands of customers across all industries.
adoption_and_market.community_size: No dedicated open-source community (proprietary service). AWS re:Post community for Q&A. AWS samples repositories on GitHub (aws-samples/amazon-bedrock-samples, aws-samples/amazon-bedrock-rag). Large AWS developer ecosystem. AWS Partners Network (APN) with numerous Bedrock-certified partners. Active AWS blog with frequent Knowledge Bases content.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: N/A — Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is a product of Amazon Web Services, a division of Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN). AWS revenue was approximately $107 billion in 2024. Bedrock is a strategic priority for AWS in the generative AI market.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Azure AI Search + Azure OpenAI Service (Microsoft, strong Office 365 integration), Google Vertex AI Search + Vertex AI (Google, strong data/analytics integration), Vectara (standalone managed RAG). Indirect competitors: LangChain/LlamaIndex (open-source frameworks requiring self-assembly), Pinecone Assistants, Cohere RAG (Command R). Key differentiators: deepest AWS service integration, multi-model flexibility (100+ FMs), S3 Vectors cost optimization, GraphRAG via Neptune, broadest vector store backend choices. Weakness: vendor lock-in to AWS, OpenSearch Serverless cost floor, less model diversity than open frameworks.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best suited for startups already on AWS (most are). Ideal for teams of 2-10 engineers who need production RAG without building infrastructure. Strong fit for: (1) B2B SaaS adding AI-powered search/Q&A over customer documents, (2) internal knowledge management tools, (3) customer support automation, (4) compliance and legal document Q&A. S3 Vectors (2025) makes it viable even for cost-sensitive early-stage startups by eliminating the OpenSearch Serverless $350/month minimum. Less ideal for: teams needing multi-cloud portability, those requiring fine-grained control over retrieval algorithms, or companies processing exclusively real-time streaming data.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Buy (use managed service) when: team lacks vector DB expertise, time-to-market is critical, already on AWS, need enterprise compliance (SOC, HIPAA, FedRAMP), or document volume exceeds what a simple solution handles. Build (self-hosted RAG) when: need multi-cloud or on-premise deployment, require custom retrieval algorithms beyond what Bedrock offers, need to minimize per-query costs at very high volumes, or want full control over the embedding-retrieval-generation pipeline. Hybrid approach: use Bedrock Knowledge Bases for ingestion and vector storage, but call the Retrieve API directly and handle generation with your own prompt engineering.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC in 1-3 days using the AWS Console wizard (no code). Production deployment in 2-4 weeks including data connector setup, chunking optimization, evaluation, and access control. Startups report 2-3 weeks from concept to production launch. Time extends to 4-8 weeks for complex enterprise deployments with multiple data sources, custom chunking via Lambda, GraphRAG, and Guardrails integration.
key_lessons: Start with S3 Vectors instead of OpenSearch Serverless to avoid the ~$350/month minimum cost floor — S3 Vectors delivers 90% savings and is sufficient for most early-stage workloads with infrequent queries.

Invest time in chunking strategy selection — the choice between fixed-size, semantic, and hierarchical chunking has more impact on RAG quality than the choice of embedding model. Use the built-in RAG evaluation (13 quality evaluators) to benchmark different configurations before production.

Watch out for hidden cost multipliers: reranking at $1/1K queries compounds when chunks exceed 100 per query, and OpenSearch Serverless idle compute runs 24/7. Model inference costs (especially for generation) typically dominate the bill — choose smaller models like Haiku for cost-sensitive applications.

Use the console-based no-code setup for rapid prototyping, but plan to move to Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform/CloudFormation) for production. The console wizard creates OpenSearch Serverless by default, which may not be the most cost-effective choice.

Leverage the built-in citation/source attribution for trust and compliance — it is a significant advantage over DIY RAG implementations and critical for regulated industries (finance, healthcare, legal).
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes. AWS Management Console provides a wizard-style no-code interface for creating knowledge bases, connecting data sources, selecting embedding models and vector stores, and testing RAG queries. Includes a built-in chat interface for validating knowledge base responses before integration into applications. No coding required for basic setup — only needed for advanced customization (custom chunking via Lambda, programmatic API access).
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy, managed AI services) and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy — cloud platform economics, scaling considerations)

confidence.data_quality: High — based on official AWS documentation, AWS blog posts, AWS re:Invent 2025 announcements, and corroborated by third-party analyses (InfoWorld, Medium, DEV Community, CloudChipr).
confidence.cross_reference: AWS official documentation (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock), AWS blog posts (aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning), AWS What's New announcements, re:Post community Q&A, third-party comparisons (Xenoss, CloudOptimo, Index.dev), LangChain and LlamaIndex official integration docs.
confidence.caveats: Pricing details for S3 Vectors are not yet fully transparent (GA December 2025, specific per-GB/per-query rates not confirmed in search results). Performance benchmarks are not publicly standardized — AWS recommends custom evaluation per use case. The service evolves rapidly (multimodal GA Nov 2025, S3 Vectors GA Dec 2025, AgentCore features 2025) so some information may become outdated quickly. Confluence/SharePoint/Salesforce connectors are limited to OpenSearch Serverless backend only. Vendor lock-in is a real concern — migrating away from Bedrock Knowledge Bases requires rebuilding the entire RAG pipeline.
confidence.security_posture: Strong compliance posture: SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, HIPAA eligible, GDPR compliant, FedRAMP High (GovCloud), PCI DSS. Data encrypted at rest (AWS KMS, supports CMK) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). AWS does not store or log prompts/completions, does not use customer data for training. Known attack surfaces: S3 bucket misconfiguration enabling RAG data poisoning (inject malicious content into knowledge base source documents), indirect prompt injection via poisoned documents persisting in agent memory, LLMJacking (unauthorized model access via compromised credentials). Mitigations: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (prompt attack detection), IAM fine-grained access control, S3 bucket policies, regular security audits, CSPM/ITDR tooling recommended.
